review_scope: All CTA sessions without confirmed conversion from the complete 101-session export.
method: Inspected action timelines and rrweb Meta/DOM/incremental event streams programmatically for every selected session; manually examined representative complete mouse/scroll/input traces and DOM field attributes. No visual playback or simulator source inspection. No form values reproduced.

clusters.name: Never begin typing after CTA; scroll briefly then exit
clusters.observed_click_pattern: Three clicks on html at (211,0), then hero CTA; no subsequent clicks.
clusters.observed_field_pattern: Only name focus, set automatically by CTA handler. Zero rrweb input events.
clusters.observed_pointer_pattern: No mouse-move batches after CTA+100ms; hover changes can be caused by scrolling content under a stationary pointer.

observations.claim: Hero CTA is clicked after substantial page traversal, not immediately on the first screen.
observations.evidence: Across selected sessions, maximum pre-CTA scroll Y is between 5732 and 7573; first CTA at 33.3–55.2 seconds.

observations.claim: No observed field-level completion obstacle in this group.
observations.evidence: All 74 have zero rrweb input, zero validation failures, zero post-CTA clicks, and only automatic name focus.
All have the same three top-edge html clicks, one hero CTA, no further clicks/input; viewport is 1280x720 for all.
observations.limitation: This is consistent with a simulator, but does not establish its decision rules or the reason for refusing to start.

hypotheses_ranked.hypothesis: Friction accumulated in long noninteractive program content or misleading card affordances affects the decision before the form.
hypotheses_ranked.basis: CTA occurs only after deep page traversal and repeated top-edge html clicks. Other early-exit review should assess card interactions.
hypotheses_ranked.test: Keep current form and CTA unchanged; shorten program module paragraphs into compact summaries while preserving modules/selectors/section order; remove pointer/hover affordances from noninteractive cards. Prefer separate experiments for summary text and affordances.
hypotheses_ranked.prediction: More of the existing CTA cohort initiates genuine name input; median program dwell/repeated dead actions decline. If only final-field errors change, this hypothesis is not supported.

hypotheses_ranked.hypothesis: Visitors decide against sharing four required fields before typing; visible required-field burden may discourage initiation.
hypotheses_ranked.basis: No one in the abandonment cohort begins typing. This is compatible with perceived burden, but not evidence of a specific field problem.
hypotheses_ranked.test: Retain mandatory fields and API; clarify near CTA/form exactly what follows submitting and why phone/email/purpose are needed, using only facts confirmed by owner. Do not invent privacy promises or response deadlines.
hypotheses_ranked.prediction: Share of CTA sessions with genuine rrweb input increases; completion among those who already start should stay similar.

hypotheses_ranked.hypothesis: Initial visible hero CTA did not create an earlier path for the current simulator population.
hypotheses_ranked.basis: All abandonment sessions click hero after having scrolled deep into the page.
hypotheses_ranked.confidence: high for observation, low for mechanism
hypotheses_ranked.test: Use session timing as diagnostic in future experiments; do not treat hero source attribution alone as evidence of shortcutting the reading path.
hypotheses_ranked.prediction: A successful early-action design would move first CTA time materially earlier and avoid deep pre-CTA traversal.

form_complexity_verdict.supported: Perceived burden before typing remains possible.
form_complexity_verdict.not_supported: The claim that users get stuck while filling fields or fail validation: no such interactions exist in the 74-session cohort.
form_complexity_verdict.cannot_prove: Underlying simulator decision rules are not observable from recordings alone.

limitations: 101 page sessions versus 100 simulator visits; one extra page session is not identified.
rrweb records rendering/interactions, not intent or simulator reasoning.
Post-CTA alignment uses server session started_at plus client elapsed time with a 100ms exclusion margin; clock offsets are small in inspected examples but exact alignment is not guaranteed.
All observed sessions are desktop 1280x720, so no mobile conclusion can be made.
